newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen Bank sees strong growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen Bank sees strong growth in '97.

text.p: Shenzhen Development Bank Co Ltd aims to have total assets of 40 billion yuan by the end of 1997, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times on Monday, a rise of 30 percent on the end-1996 figure.
The newspaper quoted bank president He Yun as saying deposits will top 30 billion yuan by end-1997, while profits will also rise sharply. He did not give a precise profit forecast.
The bank's total assets stood at 30 billion yuan at end-1996, with outstanding deposits at 22.84 billion yuan, according to the firm's 1996 annual report.
The company will continue to focus on risk control and explore new banking business, the newspaper said without elaborating.
The bank posted a net profit of 787.48 million yuan for 1996 against 435.13 million for 1995 under Chinese accounting standards.
The company, which evolved from the merger of six agricultural credit cooperatives in late 1980s, is the only mainland Chinese bank with a domestic stock exchange listing.
The firm had 1.03 billion outstanding shares at the end of 1996, consisting of 714.42 million A shares, 237.12 million institutional shares and 83.02 million state shares. (US$1 = 8.3 yuan)
